verses.text: Thus the heavens and the earth were completed in all their vast array.
And by the seventh day God had finished the work He had been doing; so on that day He rested from all His work.
Then God blessed the seventh day and sanctified it, because on that day He rested from all the work of creation that He had accomplished.
This is the account of the heavens and the earth when they were created, in the day that the LORD God made them.
Now no shrub of the field had yet appeared on the earth, nor had any plant of the field sprouted; for the LORD God had not yet sent rain upon the earth, and there was no man to cultivate the ground.
But springs welled up from the earth and watered the whole surface of the ground.
Then the LORD God formed man from the dust of the ground and breathed the breath of life into his nostrils, and the man became a living being.
And the LORD God planted a garden in Eden, in the east, where He placed the man He had formed.

Out of the ground the LORD God gave growth to every tree that is pleasing to the eye and good for food. And in the middle of the garden were the tree of life and the tree of the knowledge of good and evil.
Now a river flowed out of Eden to water the garden, and from there it branched into four headwaters:
The name of the first river is Pishon; it winds through the whole land of Havilah, where there is gold.
And the gold of that land is pure, and bdellium and onyx are found there.
The name of the second river is Gihon; it winds through the whole land of Cush.
The name of the third river is Hiddekel; it runs along the east side of Assyria. And the fourth river is the Euphrates.
Then the LORD God took the man and placed him in the Garden of Eden to cultivate and keep it.
And the LORD God commanded him, "You may eat freely from every tree of the garden,
but you must not eat from the tree of the knowledge of good and evil; for in the day that you eat of it, you will surely die."
The LORD God also said, "It is not good for the man to be alone. I will make for him a suitable helper."

And out of the ground the LORD God formed every beast of the field and every bird of the air, and He brought them to the man to see what he would name each one. And whatever the man called each living creature, that was its name.
The man gave names to all the livestock, to the birds of the air, and to every beast of the field. But for Adam no suitable helper was found.
So the LORD God caused the man to fall into a deep sleep, and while he slept, He took one of the man's ribs and closed up the area with flesh.
And from the rib that the LORD God had taken from the man, He made a woman and brought her to him.
And the man said: "This is now bone of my bones and flesh of my flesh; she shall be called 'woman,' for out of man she was taken."
For this reason a man will leave his father and mother and be united to his wife, and they will become one flesh.
And the man and his wife were both naked, and they were not ashamed.

context.author: Genesis names no author. Jewish and Christian tradition, and the New Testament’s way of speaking of “the Law of Moses” (Luke 24:44), credit the five books of the Law to Moses. Many scholars think Genesis was gathered and shaped from older sources over a long time, and a few remarks look back from a later day: “at that time the Canaanites were in the land” (Genesis 12:6).
context.genre: Narrative of beginnings (Genesis 1-11): creation, the first family, the flood and the nations, with genealogies
context.audience: Israel, God’s covenant people, learning who their God is, where the world came from and what went wrong with it
context.setting: On the seventh day God rests from all His work, and He blesses the day and makes it holy (vv.1-3). Then the story starts again, close up. “The LORD God formed man from the dust of the ground and breathed the breath of life into his nostrils” (v.7). He plants a garden in Eden, in the east, with the tree of life and the tree of the knowledge of good and evil in the middle (vv.8-9). A river flows out of Eden and splits into four, two of them the Tigris and the Euphrates (vv.10-14). The man is put in the garden “to cultivate and keep it,” and is told not to eat from the tree of knowledge: “in the day that you eat of it, you will surely die” (vv.15-17). “It is not good for the man to be alone” (v.18). The animals are brought to him to name, but none is a fit helper (vv.19-20), so God makes the woman from the man’s side, and he cries, “This is now bone of my bones and flesh of my flesh” (v.23). “The man and his wife were both naked, and they were not ashamed” (v.25).
context.custom: Here God has a new name: “the LORD God,” joining His personal name YHWH (printed LORD) to Elohim, God. The man (adam) is made from the ground (adamah), and his name keeps the link. In the ancient Near East a royal garden or park beside a temple was a sign of a king’s blessing; the same verbs used for the man’s work in the garden, to serve and to keep, are later used for the priests serving in the tabernacle (Numbers 3:7-8).
context.timelineImmediate: Chapter 3 tells how the serpent tempted the woman, how the man and woman ate from the forbidden tree, and how they were sent out of the garden.
context.timelineBible: Jesus quotes v.24 when asked about divorce: “the two will become one flesh” (Matthew 19:5), and adds, “What God has joined together, let man not separate” (Matthew 19:6). Paul uses the same verse of Christ and the church (Ephesians 5:31-32). Revelation ends with the river of the water of life and the tree of life in the new Jerusalem (Revelation 22:1-2).

translation.meaning: Ground, soil, land. Man, adam, is formed from the adamah: the earthling from the earth.
A breathing creature, a living being, a life, often translated ‘soul.’ The animals are called living creatures too (1:24); man becomes one when God breathes into him.
Help, a helper. Elsewhere the word is used mostly of God, Israel’s helper (Psalm 33:20; 121:1-2). It does not mean someone lesser. ‘Suitable’ means corresponding to him, his match.

gospelParallels.note: From the beginning the Creator made them male and female.
The first man Adam became a living being; the last Adam a life-giving spirit.
The river of the water of life and the tree of life.

mapCoords.placeName: Eden (location unknown; Genesis names the Tigris and Euphrates)

overview.summary: God rests on the seventh day, forms the man from dust and breathes life into him, sets him in the garden of Eden with one command, and makes the woman to be his partner.
overview.settingLine: A garden in Eden, in the east.
overview.placeName: Eden (location unknown; Genesis names the Tigris and Euphrates)

history.t: The Tigris and Euphrates place Eden in the world of Mesopotamia.
The personal name YHWH appears here for the first time.

customs.t: Kings planted parks to show their wealth and blessing.
To name something was to show authority over it.

archaeology.t: The Tigris and Euphrates meet near Basra; the Pishon and Gihon are not known with certainty.
Assyrian palace carvings show royal parks with streams and trees.

overview.discussion: God said, “It is not good for the man to be alone” (v.18), before anything in the world had gone wrong. Who in my life needs me not to leave them alone?
overview.book: The book of Genesis · 50 chapters (1-25 in the app so far). Beginnings: creation, the fall, the flood and the nations, then God’s promise to Abraham and his family.
overview.author: Moses, by tradition

peoplePlaces.d: Formed from dust, names the animals

historicalImage.caption: The Creation of Adam, by Michelangelo (about 1511), Sistine Chapel. God reaches out to the man He has formed: “The LORD God formed man from the dust of the ground and breathed the breath of life into his nostrils” (Genesis 2:7).

currentImage.caption: The Euphrates River below Dura-Europos in Syria. Genesis names the Tigris and the Euphrates among the four rivers that flowed out of Eden (2:14), placing the garden somewhere in the world of Mesopotamia.
